title: Let display settings survive session replication

blocks.text: Users can now pick the time zone the web app shows dates in. `DisplaySettings` lives in the HTTP session, and in production the cluster replicates every session to a second node by serializing it, so the settings must come back intact on the other node. Callers ask `timeZone()`, which returns `Optional<String>`, and fall back to the server's zone when it is empty.
Finish `setTimeZone` and `timeZone` in `src/main/java/practice/DisplaySettings.java`, adding the field they need. About three lines in total.

cases.says: a time zone the user chose is returned by timeZone()
settings with a chosen time zone serialize and come back with it
a user who never chose a time zone gets an empty Optional

origin.section: An Optional Field Breaks Serialization, and an Optional Parameter Can Still Be null

concepts: An Optional field makes a Serializable class fail at run time with NotSerializableException; keep the field nullable and return Optional from the getter.
